rows.label: A few pairs of folded socks rest on top of one folded t-shirt on a chair.
Through the air and across the walls, household appliances hum softly.
A glass ashtray holds only a single burnt match.
A sticky note clings to the corner of a cupboard.
From the street, two dogs bark briefly at each other.
A turned-off floor fan sits alone in the corner.
A pair of shoes sits right next to the door.
An analog clock ticks from somewhere.
A shoelace trails out from under the couch.
One light switch plate is missing its cover.
Books pile up under folded socks.
A large artwork piece has been put on a wall.
A stray nail clipper shines on a surface.
Keys dangle from the lock of an unlocked door.
A small flask of perfume stands just within reach.
A coat covers the back of a chair.
An unplugged charger dangles from the edge of a table.
The kitchen sink holds one soapy spoon.
The light of a car passes through the window, tracing part of the wall as it goes by.
The aroma of coffee rises from a used ceramic cup on the table.
A vertical vacuum cleaner hides in a tight corner behind a cabinet.
Next to the door, a paper bag full of trash patiently waits to be taken outside.
On the table, a water bottle with hourly markers is two hours behind.
A shiny black router points its antennas in three different directions, tiny green eyes blinking.
A bathrobe hangs from the top of an open door.
A stray necklace has been left on a counter.
An old photo on the wall captures a moment from a simpler time.
Portraits stand on a table; the pictures, as well as their subjects, are generations apart.
The faint trace of lavender hovers around a misplaced aerosol can.
A half-empty blister pack of painkillers stands guard next to a bottle of water.
The cover of a puzzle magazine faces the ceiling, its pages probably parted in an ongoing puzzle.
Neighbors laugh aloud, muffled but barely audible.
A neighbor turns on music very loudly, then lowers it an instant later.
A strange embroidery made by a local artist hangs on its hoop on the wall.
One spot on the wall gathers postcards from different places around the world, all by the same artist.
Postcards from all over the world are organized on the wall.
A cardboard box full of holiday decorations hides among other things in a closet.
From time to time, the lamp above flickers for an instant, in its final days.
One wall is painted a different color, matching the furniture.
A worn-out but solid CD sleeve is covered in teenage doodles from lives ago.
From within the walls, the muffled flow of water descends.
Two jackets and one hat hang on an elliptical bike.
The homely smell of food cooked hours ago still lingers in the air.
Pajamas are folded and resting on the lid of an empty laundry basket.
A thick candle waits for the day it might be used, its center hollowed and cold.
A broom rests against the wall, over the small mound of dust it piled up before.
The pot of a healthy plant exhales a pleasant earthy scent.
An e-reader rests on a wooden surface, the screen locked on a black-and-white image.
A salty, pleasant smell clings to the cardboard of a food-delivery package.
A wet towel has been forgotten over the back of a chair.
